frozen_note: Frozen before any detector was run on the collected data and before any return was computed. Changing any value creates a new version that cannot reuse results already seen.

primary_event.name: significant_24h_move
primary_event.price: hourly candle close (field c), Hyperliquid perpetual
primary_event.sampling: 1h; observation at hour t = close of the candle whose close_ts is t - 1 ms; the value is known only from available_at = close_ts + 1 ms
primary_event.return: R24(t) = C(t) / C(t - 24h) - 1, a simple percentage return, computed exactly from the provider decimal strings (Decimal), never rounded before classification
primary_event.operator: strict inequality on |R24|; exactly +3% or -3% is NOT a crossing
primary_event.log_return_note: Internally L24 = ln(C(t)/C(t-24h)) may be reported. R24 > 0.03 is identical to L24 > ln(1.03) = 0.0295588; R24 < -0.03 is identical to L24 < ln(0.97) = -0.0304592. Classification always uses the exact ratio C(t)/C(t-24h) against 1.03 and 0.97, so the log transform cannot move a boundary case.
primary_event.reference_selection: C(t - 24h) is the close of the observation whose close time is nearest to (t - 24h), searched only within +/- 1 h of t - 24h; ties go to the earlier observation. Selection is by distance to the 24-hour target, never by calendar day or 'latest at or before', so timestamp jitter cannot silently turn a 24-hour return into a 48-hour one (production defect RE-8). The actual elapsed time between the two observations is recorded.
primary_event.coverage_rule: VALID only if (a) the 24-hour reference exists within the tolerance and (b) no gap between consecutive available observations in [t - 24h - tolerance, t] exceeds 2 h. Otherwise LOW_COVERAGE: no classification, no crossing, no interpolation, no distant substitute.

episode.start: the first VALID crossing (UP or DOWN) when no episode is active starts an episode and emits one alert
episode.same_direction_continuation: further VALID crossings in the same direction while the episode is active belong to it (no new alert); every crossing's timestamp and observations are kept
episode.merge_after_resolution: a same-direction crossing within 24 h after the last crossing of a resolved episode re-opens that episode (no new alert; recorded as merged)
episode.opposite_direction: a VALID crossing in the opposite direction ends the active episode at that hour (resolution_reason OPPOSITE_CROSSING) and starts a new episode in the new direction with its own alert; opposite-direction episodes are never merged
episode.onset: estimated at first detection from data available then: the hour of the lowest close (UP) or highest close (DOWN) among VALID-window observations in [first_crossing_t - 24h, first_crossing_t]; ties go to the latest such hour. Uncertainty interval = [open_ts, close_ts] of that candle. Never revised with later data.
episode.first_detection: available_at of the first crossing's candle plus collection latency (0 for retrospective candle replay; reported separately when measured)
episode.confirmation: the earliest of: (a) persistence: the same-direction crossing condition is VALID and true at each of the 3 hourly closes after first detection (t+1h, t+2h, t+3h), confirmation at t+3h; (b) magnitude: |R24| >= 1.5 x threshold (= 0.045 for the primary rule) at any hour of the episode, confirmation at that hour. A LOW_COVERAGE hour breaks persistence (a).
episode.resolution: the episode ends at the 6th consecutive VALID hourly close with |R24| < 0.02; LOW_COVERAGE hours do not count and reset the run; an episode still active at the end of the scored period is OPEN
episode.magnitude: retrospective, computed only after resolution: peak excursion of closes from the onset close between onset and resolution (UP: max close / onset close - 1; DOWN: min close / onset close - 1); never available to the alert

B0.name: production LARGE_MOVE, faithful replay
B0.implementation: research/event_detector.py detect_large_moves, imported unchanged from main b48fa33
B0.input: read-only extract of production btc_data (ts, btc_price) as it exists now, including its backfilled rows
B0.schedule: called as the live pipeline does: every 6 h at 00/06/12/18 UTC with window [run - 3 d, run]; an event fingerprint is emitted once; alert time = the first run that emits it
B0.threshold: 4% absolute 24h on the first reading of each UTC day (production constants, unchanged)
B0.assets: BTC only (production has no ETH or LINK move detector, so B0 emits nothing for them)

B0h.name: production LARGE_MOVE algorithm on clean 3-hourly candle readings (algorithm-only sensitivity)
B0h.implementation: the same unchanged function and run schedule
B0h.input: for each asset, readings at 00/03/06/.../21 UTC equal to the close of the candle that closes at that tick, timestamped at available_at
B0h.purpose: separates the algorithm's own behaviour from production data defects; applied counterfactually to ETH and LINK

B1.name: primary detector
B1.rule: primary_event and episode rules above, hourly closes
B1.note: B1 on the candle data defines the reference episodes; its row checks implementation consistency only

B2.name: 4-hour detector
B2.rule: R4(t) = C(t)/C(t - 4h) - 1, UP if > +0.025, DOWN if < -0.025; reference within +/- 1 h of t - 4h; same gap rule over [t - 4h - tolerance, t]; same episode rules with confirmation at |R4| >= 0.0375 or 3-hour persistence and resolution after 6 VALID hours with |R4| < 0.0167
B2.objective: a different objective (4-hour moves); its alerts are scored against the primary 24-hour reference episodes and labelled as such, and its own episode count is reported separately

B3.name: volatility-adjusted detector (sensitivity, not a replacement for B1)
B3.rule: L24(t) = ln(C(t)/C(t - 24h)); threshold T(t) = k x sigma_1h(t) x sqrt(24); UP if L24 > T, DOWN if L24 < -T
B3.sigma: sample standard deviation of hourly log returns between consecutive VALID hourly closes, over the 720 hourly returns ending at the 24-hour reference observation (so the window (t - 24h, t] being judged is excluded)
B3.insufficient_history: fewer than 648 (90%) valid hourly returns in that 720-hour window: INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY, no classification
B3.episode: same rules with confirmation at 1.5 x T and resolution after 6 VALID hours with |L24| < (2/3) x T
